overview: A heavy AI and Tesla day. Tesla's Roadster event drew a stunt-filled demo that Musk billed as a 'flying car'. Google pushed Gemini 4 Argon and a quantum error-correction result, and Meta released open weights for Muse Spark Open. On the money side, Chamath questions how good AI revenue really is, Ramp raised at a $60B valuation, and burrytracker says the market is back in 'Fear'.

top_items.title: elonmusk - Tesla Roadster unveil: Musk says 'the future does have flying cars'; Tesla lists active aero, suction system and cold-gas thrusters
demishassabis - Gemini 4 Argon posts 97.5% on ARC-AGI-3 at $4.8K, per ARC Prize; now rolling out to Google AI Pro users in Antigravity
finkd - Meta releases weights for Muse Spark Open, billed as the most capable US open-weight model, and says it runs well on new Mac Studios
sundarpichai - Google Quantum AI demonstrates 'magic state cultivation' on Willow hardware: 40x error reduction, 99.99% logical fidelity
elonmusk - Musk says the SpaceX–Nvidia 'Star Mind' space server will reach volume production next year, and 10GW of compute could be 'maybe more'
saranormous - Greg Brockman on No Priors: OpenAI pulled 25% of its production engineers onto security only, with its top model hunting bugs
chamath - Chamath suspects 70-80% of AI company revenue comes from other VC-funded AI companies, as AI takes ~83% of US venture funding
JTLonsdale - Ramp raises $1.85B at a $60B valuation, with revenue reportedly growing over 100% year on year at multi-billion scale
